title: North Atlantic Igneous Province
summary: The North Atlantic Igneous Province is the Paleogene volcanic province of the northern North Atlantic, with magmatism normally dated to 63 to 55 Ma and traditionally tied to the Iceland hotspot. In Northern Ireland the Antrim Lava Group gives a weighted mean age of 62.63 ± 0.31 Ma, and newer uranium-lead work dates activity there from about 61.6 to 55.9 Ma. Whether a plume or rifting drove it is still contested.

uncertainty.note: Ganerød et al. (2010): NAIP magmatism normally 63 to 55 Ma; Antrim Lava Group weighted mean 62.63 ± 0.31 Ma. Cooper et al. (2026): Northern Ireland segment ca. 61.6 to 55.9 Ma, shortening its duration to 5.5 Myr. The id says 62 Ma. Years are Ma counted back from the present.
